text:
alex: Heads up — running into a weird failure in the sampleapp when switching from sync->async embed batching. Rerank endpoint is coming back with the right scores but the SDK is pairing them with the wrong queries sometimes.

maria: hmm, can you paste the request/response? also which SDK language?

alex: Node sampleapp, here's the outgoing batch (redacted):
```json
{
  "operation": "embed_batch",
  "items": [
    { "id": "q1", "text": "lookup pricing tiers" },
    { "id": "q2", "text": "how to enable dedicated" },
    { "id": "q3", "text": "rerank sampleapp bug" }
  ]
}
```
and the rerank call expects the embeddings in the same order, but what we get back from the service (observed body) is:
```json
{
  "results": [
    { "id": "q2", "vector": [0.1,0.2,..], "score": 0.87 },
    { "id": "q1", "vector": [0.05,0.3,..], "score": 0.65 },
    { "id": "q3", "vector": [0.12,0.11,..], "score": 0.43 }
  ]
}
```
but the Node helper doc says it will return `items` matching input order and we sometimes see the SDK returning vectors assoc'd to q1,q2 swapped.

ben: I reproduced locally. Looks like two issues: 1) the service-level rerank fallback merges partial batches (auth refresh triggered retry) and concatenates results from the retry path without stable sort; 2) the Node batch helper uses array index mapping assuming stable order.

jen: :thinking_face: Is this specifically when auth refresh happens? alex, did you see 401 -> silent refresh?

alex: yes, logs show an auth refresh around the same time:
```
[INFO] 12:03:22 request  id=abc123 status=401
[INFO] 12:03:23 auth-refresh token rotated
[INFO] 12:03:23 request  id=abc123 retry=1 status=200
```
The retry returned results in a different ordering (service returns by internal shard then retry gets appended).

maria: OK that maps. SDK should never rely on service order unless server promises stable ordering. We have two short fixes: a) server side: attach an input id to each item in the merged response (preserve original item.id in response entries), or b) client side: index by id before returning to caller.

ben: Quick patch idea for the Node helper: normalize response by id. Example change: after receiving `resp.results` run `const byId = new Map(resp.results.map(r => [r.id, r])); return items.map(i => byId.get(i.id));` That avoids order assumptions and also makes retries idempotent.

sdk-bot: FYI — PR #6123 rolled out a server-side merge change yesterday (can cause unsorted merge until next minor patch). Added to deploy notes.

jen: Also saw a separate edge: Python SDK previously returned `results` as list but the Node SDK renamed it to `items` in v0.9. That naming drift breaks sampleapp mapping code if teams copy snippets verbatim. We should standardize field names across SDKs and docs.

alex: Agreed. For a short-term workaround in sampleapp I swapped to id-indexing and added a unit test that shuffles server response order. Test uses this fuzz:
```js
it('preserves id mapping when server shuffles', async () => {
  const req = makeBatch(['q1','q2','q3'])
  const resp = { results: shuffle(serverGroundTruth(req.items)) }
  const normalized = normalizeById(resp.results, req.items)
  expect(normalized.map(x => x.id)).toEqual(['q1','q2','q3'])
})
```

maria: Can someone open a ticket to: 1) add id field to all response entries on the server, 2) add cross-sdk schema test that asserts field name parity (results vs items), 3) make SDK helpers resilient to reordered responses.

ben: I'll file the ticket and include traces + reproducer. Also adding a tiny e2e in the sampleapp that simulates auth refresh mid-batch.

jen: One more gotcha I found — quantized embeddings (fp16) sometimes come back as JSON arrays of strings in one path. Client code that does `Float32Array.from(vec)` blows up. We should normalize numeric types on the client too.

alex: thanks — will add a step to the onboading docs: "validate vector shapes and types" and include small sniffers: length check, numeric coercion, id presence.

ci-bot: test-runner/build  #227: sampleapp-compat-tests failed on shuffle-preserve (flaky) — rerun queued.

maria: Great catch everyone. ben open the PR for the Node helper change and add the regression test. I'll follow up with platform to add id to responses. :thumbsup:
